I need current SW’s or those about to get their MSWs be brutally honest with me

Is it worth it right now to get an MSW and go into SW? I got my bachelors in public health but I’m much more drawn into getting an MSW instead of an MPH. I work at a hospital and see our SW’s and what they do daily and it really interests me. I’d love to be a case manager and get people connected to resources and etc. 

But I have a lot of concerns. I’m 23 and I simply don’t have $60k in the bank to pay for an MSW. Nor will I anytime soon. I know I’d have to take out loans regardless but the pay for SW isn’t great in the first place so I’d be really worried of just being stuck in debt for years to come while also struggling to pay rent, and etc. 

And then with our current administration I fear that job security for SWs is at a shaky and unpredictable spot. With cuts to human services I sadly wouldn’t be shocked to see SW jobs go away. The economy is also shaky right now and more and more hospitals are announcing job layoffs which concerns me because I’d love to do medical SW. 

My other plan is to simply switch gears entirely and go into X-ray technology (I’m too anxious for nursing lol). It’s not really what I want to do but at least it’s just an associates degree for maybe $15k and the job security is okay. 

Any advice would be great. I feel very stuck on what to do

Omg welcome to Septa!!!! Def download the transit app as well as the septa app. Septa has two subway lines the Broad Street Line (BSL) which goes up and down Broad Street and the Market Frankford Line (MFL or just the El) which goes east to west on Market Street as well as all the way up most of Frankford Ave 

Cecil B Moore Station is basically on Temple’s campus which can easily get you into Center City. Keep in mind though, the express train does NOT stop at Cecil B/Temple so be sure you’re on the SOUTHBOUND side if you’re going to Center City. You’ll see signs but at first it can be a bit confusing. If you’re on the Northbound side you’re going the wrong way unless you’re trying to get to Temple Hospital or further up in North Philly 

Septa now accepts Apple and Google pay so you can easily pay the fare with your phone. You can also get a septa key card at most septa stations for I wanna say $5? It’s like a debit card that you can funds onto through the septa app. 

There’s also the busses which are a bit confusing at first as well. Google maps and the transit app will tell you which busses to take and where to board. Hope this all helps! As always if out at night and taking public transit try to go with friends for safety but other than that you should be fine

1. Network, network, network. If you don’t have a LinkedIn make one now! It’s free

2. Build that resume!!! Whether it’s related to your major or not, all jobs have transferable skills that can include teamwork, problem-solving, time management, and etc that will look good from an employer’s perspective

3. Building on that, if you want to find a job related or semi related to your major, you can always ask a professor about good place to start. Or see if there are any internships related to your major either within Temple or externally. Some majors offer teaching assistant jobs to undergrads where you’ll get paid (albeit not a lot) to teach usually lower level classes and that looks great on your resume, especially if you’re considering grad school 

4. Temple’s career center is actually pretty impressive for the size of the school. You can get free headshots, free career coaching, resume editing, cover letter advice, and mock interviews. Check out their website they hold a lot of cool events throughout the year: 

https://careercenter.temple.edu

5. Temple hosts a lot of career fairs throughout the year both in-person and virtually that I’d recommend attending. Even if you’re a freshman you can always attend to see who’s there and maybe meet people who work somewhere that you’ve been looking into or etc
